# Introduction

This book is intended to be used as a starting point for those learning about railway signalling for the first time. It is designed to give a basic overview and understanding of signalling, and an introduction to the railway.

It is essentially my attempt at creating the book I wished I had when I first started.

## Who the book is for

The book is intended for those who are new to railway signalling, including those beginning work in signalling and telecommunications (S&T). It introduces the railway equipment, its purpose and the relationships between systems before moving into more detailed equipment descriptions.

## How to use the book

Read the opening chapters in sequence. [Railway locations](railway-locations.qmd) introduces line names, directions and location references. [Railway signalling](railway-signalling.qmd) introduces train separation, control and the main equipment and system relationships. [History of signalling](history-of-signalling.qmd) explains how those principles developed. The later chapters develop trackwork, points, signals, circuit reading, relays and the systems that connect them.

For each item, establish what it does, how it fits into the wider signalling system and what happens when it fails to perform its function.

Use [Useful other sources of information](useful-sources-of-information.qmd) to find references for further study. Practical work requires the applicable controlled documentation, local arrangements and competence; this introductory book does not define test limits, maintenance intervals or authority to work.
